Flow Systems - In the Project Area, the potentiometric heads decrease in successively deeper units of the Tongue River member. There is a relatively high vertical head gradient and a relatively low lateral or horizontal gradient in the ground-water flow system. The flow systems are continuous under the higher topographic features but towards discharge areas are separated by local ground-water divides. Near discharge areas, the flow systems become discontinuous. In these areas, there is lateral groundwater flow through units having relatively high horizontal permeability, compared to the relatively low vertical permeability of underlying rock. The comparatively rapid lateral flow through the more permeable coal beds, clinker, and sandstones tends to cause the overlying strata to drain back away from points of discharge. This makes the zone of saturation discontinuous in and near the discharge areas. The ground-water divides, which locally separate the flow systems, migrate in response to changes in potentiometric heads in the flow system.
Recharge to the shallow systems in Tract II is by infiltration of rainfall on the area. Tract II is topographically higher than adjacent areas, so that regional flow cannot take place. Ground water in Tract III is recharged by precipitation on the area; but in addition, there is lateral flow of ground water into the tract from recharge areas in the topographically higher Little Wolf Mountains to the southeast. In Tract II, the Rosebud-McKay has burned on much of the tract; where it is present, the flow in the Rosebud-McKay coal bed aquifer is largely down dip to the northeast towards Sarpy Creek and Spring Creek.
